rulings.challenge_claim: The row gives no disclosure for keeping a self-contained blessing address to the Rechabites under the symbolic-act category rather than a more specific oracle type, since no command, performance, or re-enactment of the wine test falls in its two verses.
rulings.grounds: The bytes tie these two verses to the act rather than away from it. The span opens on the tag וּלְבֵ֨ית הָרֵכָבִ֜ים אָמַ֣ר יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ (oshb:Jer.35.18, byte), turning the address to the very household whose refusal the wine test staged, and the promise at oshb:Jer.35.19 answers the obedience named in the same verse; both quoted runs are whole verses at byte tier. The closed 13-value unit-type vocabulary carries this chapter's Rechabite material as its own listed symbolic-act example, so the label is the operative category here, not a departure from it, and the one-sentence disclosure the challenge invokes is owed only where a row's bytes push it OFF the operative category, which is the opposite of what these bytes do. The ruled granularity likewise holds a symbolic act's command, performance, and interpretation as ONE unit unless a tier-1 seam intervenes: the two tier-1 seams inside this chapter (the verse-initial word-event onset at oshb:Jer.35.12, one of the 21 verses of that shape, and the verse-initial speaker-and-addressee tag at oshb:Jer.35.18) split the complex into rows without changing the operative category of its parts. Nothing else in the row is disturbed on re-derivation: the koh-amar at both verses stands in Jeremiah's named mouth, the frame-owner requirement met in a book where the full divine formula is also put in a false prophet's mouth (sweep: 2 verses, 28:2 and 28:11); the divine-title key is byte-correct at both, יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.35.18, byte) and יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Jer.35.19, byte), members of the 32-verse full-stack signature; and the mark accounting is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 35:18, PE at MT 35:19, a true absence at the front-seam verse MT 35:17; 0 paseq segs and 0 variant notes in MT 35:18-35:19, single-witness WLC, tier-3 weak in the Prophets). The challenge cites no byte at all: it rests on a category-policy reading alone, which under the symmetric evidence rule is as defective as a row resting on a marker alone.

rulings.challenge_claim: The rival splitting Jer.36.2-4 from Jer.36.5-7 is refused on a ground the span's own splice supplies against it, a speaker-and-addressee change falling at Jer.36.5; the frame prose miscounts the book's word-event shapes as two; the literature type carries an unsourced reading ordinal; and the two overlapping runs at Jer.36.1 are glossed past their own extent.
rulings.grounds: All four parts verify on re-derivation, and two of them reach further than charged. (1) The refusal ground is byte-contested exactly where it matters: oshb:Jer.36.2 opens קַח לְךָ֮ מְגִלַּת סֵפֶר֒ (oshb:Jer.36.2, byte), a second-person imperative inside the divine speech introduced by the word clause of oshb:Jer.36.1, while the proposed seam verse opens וַיְצַוֶּ֣ה יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ אֶת בָּר֖וּךְ לֵאמֹ֑ר (oshb:Jer.36.5, byte), a fresh speech tag with a new speaker and a new addressee. An explicit addressee or scene shift is a tier-1 internal cut class, so the rival is refused on the one term the bytes hand it; the ground's other two terms hold (no date frame and no word-event formula stand between oshb:Jer.36.2 and oshb:Jer.36.7). NEW, same field: the ground also misassigns the mouth, since verses 2 and 3 are the divine commission to Jeremiah, not part of 'the single unbroken commission Jeremiah gives Baruch', which begins only at oshb:Jer.36.4-Jer.36.5. (2) The shape count is wrong against a three-member object: the byte-derived frame census carries THREE never-blended word-event shapes (sweep: 21 verses of the vayehi-debar-YHWH shape; 11 verses of the prose-sermon superscription shape; 4 verses of the OAN/topical header shape). NEW: the two-shape wording stands in TWO fields, the boundary rationale as well as the device note, so the cure is one edit over both. Correcting the challenge's illustration without disturbing its digit: the omitted 4-verse shape is not the nearest in wording, since this verse's own clause הָיָ֞ה הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.36.1, byte) shares hadavar and the me'et-YHWH tail with the 11-verse superscription shape the row does name, while the omitted shape reads debar-YHWH without that tail. (3) The ordinal: the only reading in the span is the infinitive complement לִקְרֹ֥א בַסֵּ֛פֶר (oshb:Jer.36.8, byte) under the finite וַיַּ֗עַשׂ (oshb:Jer.36.8, byte) in a dateless compliance summary, while the finite narrated reading וַיִּקְרָ֨א בָר֥וּךְ בַּסֵּ֛פֶר (oshb:Jer.36.10, byte) falls outside it, so 'first publicly read' settles in-span what the bytes leave held; the heuristic flag standing on that word is a true positive, not a false one. NEW: that ordinal is one chain with the ordinal in the unit spanning Jer.36.9-Jer.36.13, and the two must be cured together. (4) Gloss extent: the first run at oshb:Jer.36.1 ends at הָיָ֞ה הַדָּבָ֤ר (oshb:Jer.36.1, byte) yet its rendering carries 'this', whose token הַזֶּה֙ (oshb:Jer.36.1, byte) lies outside the run; the second run begins at הַזֶּה֙ (oshb:Jer.36.1, byte) yet its rendering carries 'came', whose token הָיָ֞ה (oshb:Jer.36.1, byte) lies outside it. Not disturbed: the onset is a verse-initial date frame, so classified among the 19 candidate sites of the byte-derived date object, and the mark set is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 36:3 and MT 36:8, the preceding PE at MT 35:19; 0 paseq segs and 0 variant notes in MT 36:1-36:8, single-witness WLC, tier-3 weak).
rulings.remedy: 1) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the clause 'with no addressee change, date frame, or fresh word-event formula falling between them' with a ground that names the speaker-and-addressee change at Jer.36.5 and rests the refusal on the frame-plus-speech default (an embedded commission stays with the narrative frame that reports it); in the same edit correct 'the single unbroken commission Jeremiah gives Baruch' so that verses 2-3 read as the divine commission to Jeremiah. TEST the cure must pass (the test that killed the original): read the replacement against the speech tag standing at oshb:Jer.36.5, it must stay true with that tag in view. 2) boundary_rationale AND device_notes: replace 'neither of the book's two named word-event shapes' and 'the book's two named word-event formulas' with the three-shape census, each shape carrying its verse digit; one edit covering both fields. TEST: the sentence must name three shapes with three digits and still hold this onset apart from all of them. 3) literature_type_guess: drop 'first' from 'first publicly read', or add the one-sentence disclosure that the in-span reading is an infinitive complement inside a dateless compliance summary while the narrated reading stands at Jer.36.10; cure this together with the ordinal in the unit spanning Jer.36.9-Jer.36.13, as a paired ordinal cure rather than a spot fix. TEST: no ordinal may remain that the verb forms at Jer.36.8 and Jer.36.10 cannot settle. 4) boundary_rationale: re-cut both renderings at oshb:Jer.36.1 to their splice extents. TEST: no rendering may contain an English word whose Hebrew token stands outside the run it is paired with.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both boundaries are byte-sound, but two content claims outrun the bytes: a second reading event at Jer.36.10, and a full-year interval between the two dated notices.
rulings.grounds: Both hold, and each reaches one field further than charged. Interval: the earlier notice carries בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הָרְבִיעִ֔ת (oshb:Jer.36.1, byte) with no month token, while this row's own onset carries בַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַ֠חֲמִשִׁית together with בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַתְּשִׁעִ֔י (oshb:Jer.36.9, byte), a year and a ninth month. With the earlier notice's month unstated in both witnesses the elapsed time is undetermined, so 'a full year on' is not sourceable from the bytes. NEW: the same unsourced interval stands a second time in literature_type_guess ('the year-later public reading'), so the cure is a two-field edit. Ordinal: the reading of the scroll stands as a finite verb once in this stretch, וַיִּקְרָ֨א בָר֥וּךְ בַּסֵּ֛פֶר (oshb:Jer.36.10, byte); the earlier report is the infinitive complement לִקְרֹ֥א בַסֵּ֛פֶר under the finite וַיַּ֗עַשׂ (oshb:Jer.36.8, byte) in a dateless compliance summary, so whether Jer.36.10 is a second event or the narration of the summarized one is a held reading, and 'Baruch's own second reading' settles it silently; the same clause also attributes the reading to 'verses 9 and 10' where the reading verb stands at Jer.36.10 alone and Jer.36.9 carries the fast proclamation. NEW: this ordinal is one chain with 'first publicly read' in the unit spanning Jer.36.1-Jer.36.8 and with this row's own device-note phrase 'the first writing-and-reading scene', three sites resting on one undisclosed reading. Severity stays low because nothing here moves a seam: the onset is a verse-initial date frame among the 19 candidate sites of the byte-derived date object; a real addressee turn stands at the rear seam (the relay is to the officials at oshb:Jer.36.13, the sending is to Baruch at oshb:Jer.36.14); the span's mark-absence statement is true (0 PE, 0 SAMEKH, 0 paseq segs, 0 variant notes in MT 36:9-36:13, single-witness WLC) with the preceding SAMEKH at MT 36:8 correctly typed; and the row already sits at reduced confidence with its frontier flagged.
rulings.remedy: 1) boundary_rationale: replace 'a fresh date frame, a full year on from the row before' with the byte-stated dating, a fourth-year notice carrying no month against a fifth-year, ninth-month notice with the interval undetermined, and apply the same correction to literature_type_guess's 'year-later'; one edit over both fields. TEST the cure must pass: every temporal statement must be resolvable from the two notices' own year and month tokens alone. 2) strongest_rejected_alternative: drop the ordinal in 'Baruch's own second reading', or carry a one-sentence disclosure that the earlier reading stands as an infinitive complement inside a dateless compliance summary; fix the same clause's verse attribution to Jer.36.10; pair the edit with the ordinal in the unit spanning Jer.36.1-Jer.36.8 and with this row's device_notes phrase. TEST: no ordinal may remain that the verb forms at Jer.36.8 and Jer.36.10 cannot settle.

rulings.challenge_claim: Converging: the machine-readable word-event key tags this row's opening formula as the book's non-initial occurrence though the verse opens on it, and the count-only paseq at the closing verse goes undisclosed inside a field that already walks that layer. Added by one item only: the rival is refused for lack of a fresh formula at the exact verse where the row's own rationale names two, and the closing verse is called Baruch's compliance though the splice fronts Jeremiah.
rulings.grounds: The two items converge on the SAME two defects (1 and 2 below); one of them adds two further, DISTINCT defects (3 and 4). (1) Position: oshb:Jer.36.27 opens וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.36.27, byte), verse-initial. The byte-derived census carries this shape at 21 verses, 20 of them verse-initial, with the single non-initial site at oshb:Jer.42.7, whose bytes open on the separate temporal clause וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת יָמִ֑ים (oshb:Jer.42.7, byte) before the formula. The key therefore asserts a second non-initial site against a one-site fact, in the machine-readable field, and contradicts the row's own rationale, which calls the same verse the opening of the reply. Tier-1, byte. (2) Disclosure symmetry: the mark inventory records BOTH a SAMEKH and one paseq seg at MT 36:32. The field cites the paseq at MT 36:27, cites the SAMEKH at MT 36:32, walks the closing verses, and adds a true absence statement for MT 36:30, so the paseq layer is engaged for this span and left incomplete at exactly one coordinate (single-witness WLC, count-only, no intra-verse position claimed). (3) The rival splitting Jer.36.29-31 from Jer.36.27-28 is refused for 'no fresh formula marking an inner seam' while the row's own rationale names two at that seam: כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.36.29, byte) and לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.36.30, byte). The ground that actually carries the refusal is frame ownership: at oshb:Jer.36.29 the formula stands inside the divine instruction to Jeremiah, וְעַל יְהוֹיָקִ֤ים מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ תֹּאמַ֔ר (oshb:Jer.36.29, byte), so the mouth does not change across the seam, and a koh-amar onset cuts only WITH a frame-owner change. (4) Agency: the closing splice fronts Jeremiah, וְיִרְמְיָ֜הוּ לָקַ֣ח מְגִלָּ֣ה אַחֶ֗רֶת וַֽיִּתְּנָהּ֮ (oshb:Jer.36.32, byte), with Baruch first the recipient of the scroll and only then the one who writes on it, so 'Baruch's own compliance' misreads the subject of the two finite verbs the row itself quotes. (5) NEW: in the same rationale a byte tier label stands on a bare coordinate at oshb:Jer.36.31 with no Hebrew run quoted, occupying the splice-and-rendering slot every other citation in that field fills with a spliced run, so the byte assertion has nothing to certify. The boundary itself is untouched: a verse-initial word-event onset is the stronger tier-1 warrant, the SAMEKH citations at MT 36:29, MT 36:31 and MT 36:32 and the preceding close at MT 36:26 all match under the right type, and 0 variant notes fall in MT 36:27-36:32.
rulings.remedy: 1) observed_substrate_signals: replace the key word_event.vayehi_debar_yhwh_non_initial with the verse-initial key of the same shape. TEST the cure must pass: no row whose span excludes Jer.42.7 may carry a non-initial word-event key, the census fixing that site at one. 2) device_notes: name the count-only paseq at MT 36:32 beside the SAMEKH already cited (single-witness, no position claimed). TEST: once a field engages the seg layer for a span, every coordinate in that span carrying a seg appears; sweep the span rather than spot-fixing the one verse. 3) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 'no fresh formula marking an inner seam' with the frame-ownership ground, the mouth not changing because the formula at Jer.36.29 stands inside the divine instruction to Jeremiah. TEST: the replacement must stay true when read against both formulas the rationale names at Jer.36.29 and Jer.36.30. 4) boundary_rationale: rename the agent of Jer.36.32 (Jeremiah takes and gives; Baruch receives and then writes), and either splice the run for oshb:Jer.36.31 or drop the byte tier label from that bare coordinate. TEST: every byte tier label in the field stands on a quoted run, and every named agent is the subject of the verb quoted beside it.

rulings.challenge_claim: The larger-unit rival is refused on a ground the row's own full-verse splice contradicts, these two verses being dense with personal names, and the name-form disclosure carries a recurrence claim with no sweep digit while under-naming the attested spellings.
rulings.grounds: (1) Byte-refuted as charged: the opening verse names five persons in one clause chain, צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בֶּן יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ תַּ֗חַת כָּנְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן יְה֣וֹיָקִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.37.1, byte) and נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל (oshb:Jer.37.1, byte), and the prophet is named at oshb:Jer.37.2; both witnesses agree, “Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned as king instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.” (web:Jer.37.1). The row quotes both verses in full at byte tier, so the denial is contradicted from inside the row, and it is the half doing the work against the following verse. (2) NEW: the ground's surviving term does not discriminate either. Neither of these verses is among the 19 candidate sites of the byte-derived date object and neither carries a year token, but neither does the verse the rival would fold them into: oshb:Jer.37.3 opens וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֜הוּ (oshb:Jer.37.3, byte) with no date token and no place in that inventory. So the dateless term is true of the span and equally true of what it is contrasted with; the whole ground needs replacing, not half of it. What genuinely separates them is byte-visible: a summary report of the reign and of a general failure to hear, against a narrated sending of two named envoys carrying a request. (3) Upheld: the rationale calls the reign 'dated to a king' installed by Babylon, where the relative clause identifies the installer and the verse carries no date token at all. (4) Upheld, with the framing corrected: the device note says the resh-family spelling 'recurs through the chapters ahead' with no digit and no unit named, in a field that does supply a digit (sweep: 3 verses) for the predecessor's Coniah form, while that spelling stands in 29 verses. The under-naming is real, the book carrying FOUR live spellings (the resh family at 29 verses plus its plene byform at 49:28, which rides a doubled variant note; the nun family at 6 verses plus the vav-less defective form at 28:11 and 28:14), but the corrected finding is a disclosure gap rather than a stated miscount: the sentence asserts no count, it names one alternative indefinitely and leaves two attested spellings unnamed. (5) Not disturbed: the Coniah digit is right token-bound (3 verses: 22:24, 22:28, 37:1) and the three name forms for this one king match the inventory; the onset is a wayyiqtol accession clause and not a word-event formula of any of the three shapes; and the mark statement is true (0 PE, 0 SAMEKH, 0 paseq segs, 0 variant notes in MT 37:1-37:2, single-witness WLC) with the preceding SAMEKH at MT 36:32 correctly typed. Severity stays medium: the row stands at high confidence on a rejected alternative whose stated ground fails on both of its terms.
rulings.remedy: 1) strongest_rejected_alternative: strike 'with no named individual or dated moment' and rest the refusal on the byte-visible contrast, a summary regnal notice with a general hearing report against the narrated sending of named envoys with a request at Jer.37.3. TEST the cure must pass (the test that killed the original): read the replacement against the five personal names standing in oshb:Jer.37.1 AND against the datelessness of oshb:Jer.37.3, it must survive both. 2) boundary_rationale: strike 'dated' from the installer clause; no date token stands in the verse and this site is not among the classified date-header candidates. TEST: no date word may remain in a sentence whose verse carries no year or month token. 3) device_notes: give the resh-family recurrence its digit and unit (sweep: 29 verses) and name the remaining attested spellings, the plene resh-family byform at 49:28 and the two nun-family forms (6 verses; the vav-less defective at 28:11 and 28:14), or say plainly that one alternative among four attested spellings is named here. TEST: every name-form sentence names its spelling and carries a digit with its unit, matching the digit discipline the same field already applies to the predecessor's name form.
